subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw add enrolled-speaker verification to native/realtime voice input, and should the first design be core-native, plugin/API-led, or deferred to external experimentation?
rationale: This cannot be safely resolved by source inspection because it changes command authorization, sensitive voice-profile storage, provider audio egress, and cross-platform voice UX.

options.title: Design Core Speaker Gate First
options.body: Define a native/realtime speaker-gating contract, storage model, provider policy, fallback behavior, and tests before accepting implementation PRs.

options.title: Prototype As Plugin/API Work
options.body: Use this issue to identify missing plugin or provider hooks and keep core changes limited to extension points until a concrete package proves the approach.

options.title: Defer As Out Of Scope
options.body: Leave current wake-word, push-to-talk, and Talk behavior unchanged until the voice roadmap prioritizes biometric-like enrollment and security review.

recommendation.title: Design Core Speaker Gate First
recommendation.body: Define a native/realtime speaker-gating contract, storage model, provider policy, fallback behavior, and tests before accepting implementation PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is repeated recent work across macOS Voice Wake, push-to-talk, Talk runtime, and Talk docs/config surfaces.
